info.title: LicenseGraph API
info.summary: Check creative licences against a project, then pay the creators.
info.description:
An AI agent reads licences and proposes the cheapest bundle. A deterministic rules engine verifies it against the project and rejects anything that breaks a term. A person approves, PayPal Orders and Payouts settle in the Sandbox, and a Licence Passport lets anyone check the result.

Money moves only after a person approves. A run an agent starts with `handoff: true` cannot be approved or paid until a person takes control with the one-time claim link. Approve, pay, capture, payouts and refund need the `lg_owner` cookie of the browser that started (or claimed) the run.

post.description: Model Context Protocol, Streamable HTTP, stateless. Point an MCP client at this URL to use `check_licence_bundle`, `cheapest_compliant_bundle`, `what_if_brief`, `licence_end_dates`, `start_licence_purchase` and `get_purchase_status`, and the `buy_licences` prompt. Requests are JSON-RPC and must accept both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. An agent can start a purchase but cannot approve or pay it: that needs the claim link a person opens.

post.summary: Answer a gap request with a licensor's revised licence
post.description: Adds the revised licence to what the run read and checks everything again as a new run (`meta.revisedFrom` names this one). The earlier run is unchanged. Nothing is bought: only a bundle that passes the rules can be approved and paid.

400.description: The run is not finished, already has a payment, or the revision is invalid.

403.description: This run belongs to another browser.

post.summary: Check the same licences against a changed brief
post.description: Makes a what-if real: starts a new run on the licences this run already read (nothing is read again) against the changed brief (`meta.rebriefedFrom` names this run). The earlier run is unchanged. Nothing is bought: only a bundle that passes the rules for the changed brief can be approved and paid.

400.description: The run is not finished, already has a payment, or the change is invalid.

403.description: This run belongs to another browser.

post.description: Called by PayPal, not by clients. Each delivery is acted on only after PayPal confirms its signature for the configured webhook id (`PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID`). `CHECKOUT.ORDER.APPROVED` captures the run's approved order, so closing the tab after approving still completes the purchase; `PAYMENT.PAYOUTSBATCH.*` refreshes payout status; `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REFUNDED` and `PAYMENT.CAPTURE.REVERSED` for a refund the app did not make are written to the ledger, and the Licence Passport then fails its payment-standing check. Other events are acknowledged and ignored.

200.description: Verified and handled, or verified and not relevant.

400.description: Missing signature headers, or the body is not a JSON event.

401.description: PayPal did not confirm the signature.

502.description: PayPal could not be reached to verify; it will deliver again.

503.description: Webhooks are not configured on this server.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 description of this API.

ownerCookie.name: lg_owner
ownerCookie.description: An unguessable id set when a browser starts or claims a run. Only that browser may approve, pay, refund or list the run.

commercial.description: True if the project earns or promotes money.

territories.description: Where the project is released: ["WORLD"] or country codes such as "US".

termMonths.description: How many months the assets are needed.

budgetCents.description: Budget in the smallest currency unit.

currency.description: Budget and settlement currency; USD if omitted.

canCredit.description: False if the project cannot credit creators.

evidence.description: Quotes from the licence text that support the terms.

Offer.description: One licence offer read from a licence document, with the quotes that back each term.

hash.description: SHA-256 over the event and prevHash; changing any event breaks every hash after it.

runDate.description: The date offers were checked against when the run started (YYYY-MM-DD).

awaitingPerson.description: An agent started this run and no person has taken control yet, so it cannot be approved or paid.

revisedFrom.description: The run whose gap requests this one answers, with a licensor's revised licence added.

rebriefedFrom.description: The run whose brief this one changed: the same licences, checked against a different brief.

candidates.description: Every offer read from the licences.

rounds.description: How many proposals the agent made before the rules engine accepted one.

bundle.description: The verified bundle. Absent until the rules engine accepts a proposal.

analysis.description: Every offer checked against every rule, the price-only comparison, requirement costs and gaps.
